subject: Breach response & dataflow clauses — DPA redline
body:
From: procurement@catalystcloud.com
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 08:12:00 -0500
Subject: DPA redline — breach notification & subprocessor dataflow

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week — CatalystCloud product and security teams are aligned to proceed, but we hit two gating items in the DPA redline (attached). We need concrete language and an evidence workflow to satisfy procurement + legal before we can route for signature.

Open items:
- Notification timeline: the redline currently says Redwood will provide "prompt" notice. Our policy requires an initial notification window of 72 hours from discovery for incidents affecting customer data, with an interim update at 7 days and a remediation summary within 30 days where feasible. Is Redwood able to commit to a defined 72-hour initial notification plus the follow-up cadence?
- Subprocessor evidence & cross-border transfers: the DPA allows use of subprocessors. Catalyst needs a short description of how Redwood notifies customers of new subprocessors processing EU-origin data and the standard method for transferring evidence (logs, timeline, SOC artifacts) in the event of an incident. Do you support a direct evidence handover to our security team, or do you require third-party escrow or an auditor-to-auditor transfer?

Attached: Catalyst_DPA_Redline_v1.pdf (pdf, 420 KB)

Can you please route this to your legal/security leads and send back suggested clause language and a sample evidence-request flow by EOD Friday (Feb 18)? If you need to loop in someone else at Redwood please cc them.

Appreciate it,

Lina Morales
Sr. Procurement Manager | CatalystCloud
procurement@catalystcloud.com

-----

From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: procurement@catalystcloud.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline — breach notification & subprocessor dataflow

Lina — thanks for the clear asks and the redline. Looping in Marissa (Legal) and Priyom (Security Ops) to propose specific language and the evidence flow.

High-level answers now so you have context: we can commit to a defined, contractual 72-hour initial notification window for incidents that meet personal data exposure thresholds. Practically:
- Initial notification: within 72 hours of Redwood’s confirmed detection of unauthorized access to customer data; notification will include scope, affected services, and immediate mitigations where known.
- Interim updates: we can send a status note at 7 days and an expected remediation summary within 30 days; if forensic work requires longer, we commit to regular updates until closed.
- Evidence handover: Redwood prefers direct, authenticated transfer of redacted logs and forensic timelines to named security contacts at the customer. For sensitive artifacts (raw disk images), we use an auditor-to-auditor exchange or an HSM/KMS-backed escrow process on request; we also host a secure SFTP bucket for document exchange when appropriate.

I asked Marissa and Priyom to propose contract wording and to attach our incident evidence process doc so you can see the typical turnaround and formats. I’ll send one consolidated suggestion shortly.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: procurement@catalystcloud.com
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 09:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline — breach notification & subprocessor dataflow

Lina / Catalyst team — attaching a short proposed clause and a recommended evidence-request workflow. I kept the language concise so it can slot into your redline with minimal edits.

Proposed DPA language (suggestion) — replace existing "prompt" language with:
"Notification: Redwood shall notify Customer without undue delay and, in any event, within 72 hours of becoming aware of a confirmed security incident that results in unauthorized access to Customer Personal Data. Notification shall include a description of the nature and scope of the incident, the categories of Personal Data affected, the steps taken to mitigate the incident, and the identity of known affected subprocessors where applicable. Redwood shall provide interim status updates at least once within seven (7) days following initial notification and a remediation summary within thirty (30) days, subject to permitted limitations for ongoing forensic investigations."

Evidence transfer addendum (suggestion):
"Evidence transfer: Upon Customer request, Redwood will provide reasonably requested forensic artifacts and logs pertinent to the incident via a mutually agreed secure channel to named security contacts. Where artifacts contain highly sensitive raw data, Redwood will, at Customer's request, facilitate an auditor-to-auditor exchange or provide access to an encrypted escrow repository. Redwood's standard evidence transfer SLA is: initial artifact deliverables within 10 business days of a validated request, with prioritized follow-up for scope expansion."

Notes on subprocessors: we propose a 10-business-day notification for new subprocessors that will process EU-origin personal data, and the option for Customer to request additional documentation (e.g., subprocessors' SCCs, SOC reports) within 20 business days of notification. We include a carve-out for emergency deployments where notice may precede onboarding.

Attachment: security-evidence-process.docx (docx, 85 KB) — contains the practical steps, expected artifact formats (redacted logs, timeline csv, hashed disk checksums) and contact template for evidence requests.

Priyom, flagged for any ops clarifications.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: legal@catalystcloud.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@catalystcloud.com
Date: Fri, 17 Feb 2028 14:20:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline — breach notification & subprocessor dataflow

Marissa / Connor — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed language. Our security counsel reviewed the draft and the evidence workflow and prefers the 72-hour initial window plus the 10-business-day artifact SLA you suggested. Two follow-ups before we finalize: 

1) Can Redwood add a short sentence confirming that evidence transfers will preserve chain-of-custody metadata and a signed transfer manifest for any auditor-to-auditor exchanges?
2) For subprocessors, we request an explicit mechanism where Catalyst may opt-in to receiving notifications for any new subprocessor that will process EU-derived personal data for the life of the contract. A 10-business-day notice is fine as long as we get a named contact and a simple opt-in checkbox in the vendor portal or via email.

If you can confirm both and send a redline we can complete internal approvals and route to execs for signature.

Best,
Elena Park
Legal Counsel | CatalystCloud
legal@catalystcloud.com
